text:
sre-bot: ALERT: nodepool 'gpu-rt-1' in prod has desired=12 actual=8 — 4 nodes terminated unexpectedly, autoscaler couldn't replace (capacity error) :rotating_light:

maria: seeing higher inference errors for some jobs, traced to GPU pod evictions. autoscaler logs show 'Insufficient capacity' from cloud provider.

kevin: checking gitops sync — ci-gitops-bot pinged earlier, last sync failed during ASG update.

ci-gitops-bot: sync failed for cluster/redwood-prod: terraform apply exit code 1. Error: "InsufficientInstanceCapacity: The requested instance type is temporarily unavailable in the requested Availability Zone."

jamal: TL;DR: us-west-2 has spot/instance shortages for g5.* right now. TF attempted to add 4 g5.xlarge nodes and cloud returned capacity error.

anika: can we fallback to g4dn or a different AZ? Prod policy avoids spot, but on-demand g4dn should be OK for short term. Perf will be ~15% worse per-token.

maria: we need a short mitigation plan: 1) stop automated GitOps sync for this change, 2) open a PR to change instance type to g4dn.xlarge as a temporary patch, 3) manual scale-up in cloud console if possible, 4) monitor inference latency/error.

kevin: I paused the automated reconcile for the nodepool in GitOps (flagged in the repo). Created draft PR: https://git.redwood.dev/r/redwood-infra/pulls/3456 to swap to g4dn.xlarge for gpu-rt-1 (draft until we validate).

jamal: I'll try manual replacement: cordon & drain the 4 empty nodes, then create 4 on-demand g4dn via cloud console as a stopgap. Docs: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data.

anika: watch the model-serving HPA and KV-cache pods — draining may reshuffle heavy tasks. Throttle rollout to avoid mass restart.

maria: also check RBAC/taints — noticed earlier we added a taint "gpu:reserved=true:NoSchedule" in a recent PR; if new nodes aren't getting the taint from cloud-init the autoscaler might consider them incompatible. That could explain autoscaler not attaching them to the pool.

kevin: good catch — terraform module changed taint key name in #3340 last week. I can add a quick patch to ensure taints are consistent across old/new node templates in the PR.

ci-gitops-bot: note: when applying nodepool template changes the controller recreates instance templates; if cloud capacity fails, operations will partially apply — ensure we have rollback.

jamal: manual plan executed: cordoned and drained 3 nodes, created 3 g4dn on-demand instances and joined them to the ASG. Pods started rescheduling, inference error rate dropped by ~60%. Still 1 node pending.

maria: opening an incident tracking thread in incidents channel and tagging infra-sre for postmortem. For now action items: - kevin: finish PR to harmonize taint + instance type (3456). - jamal: finish the last node replacement and validate logs. - anika: run perf smoke tests against canary route and watch per-token latency.

anika: running smoke now, routing 10% traffic to patched pool. Initial p50 increased from 82ms -> 95ms, p95 from 210ms -> 250ms. Acceptable for 1 hour fallback.

kevin: PR updated to ready -> please review: https://git.redwood.dev/r/redwood-infra/pulls/3456 (includes taint fix + instance type fallback + commit to pin desired capacity).

maria: once PR merges, we'll re-enable GitOps sync and let it converge. Schedule postmortem to decide longer-term tolerances for instance-type fallbacks and autoscaler policy (spot vs on-demand fallback).

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-487 — assigned to eng-infra. Severity: S2.

maria: thanks all — keep this thread updated with any regressions. :thumbsup:
